## 2026-08-02 - RM-146 + RM-147 CLOSED (relocated from ROADMAP 2026-08-02)

Relocated VERBATIM the same session both rows CLOSED, when ROADMAP.md hit 97 percent of its
81920-byte budget. Compact pointers remain in ROADMAP.md. RM-146 is the memory-ceiling
measurement (LEDGER 1171); RM-147 is the OBS Display Capture decision that unblocked G6-03
(LEDGER 1170). Both carry refuted-claim records worth keeping: RM-147's original BSOD risk
paragraph cited a memory that had been deleted, and RM-146's 810 MB peak was wrongly
hypothesised as resolution flips before being measured as post-game work.

- **RM-146 CLOSED 2026-08-02 - the ceiling was wrong, nothing leaks; raised 300/500 -> 700/1200 (`core/resource_manager.py:46-62`), pinned by `tests/test_resource_manager_ceiling_rm146.py` (7 tests, TDD - all 4 substantive ones were RED at the old ceiling first).** **The ratchet question is ANSWERED and REFUTED:** a second full ARAM on the SAME process (pid 21348) landed in-game n=29 mean 538.9 / min 532.3 / **max 547.9 against game 1's max 547.6 - the same roof within 0.3 MB** - and committed memory moved 1007.3 -> 1031.7 MB across that entire second match. Per-game residue would have added ~835 MB; game 2's START cost only +55 MB RSS / +28 MB committed against game 1's +392 / +835. So the game-start step is a ONE-TIME lazy warm-up that is REUSED. **THE 787-810 MB PEAK IS EXPLAINED, and my first hypothesis for it was WRONG.** I guessed the G6-04 desktop-resolution flips; the actual cause is POST-GAME work - a deliberately restarted RC measured **804.9 MB RSS / 1266.1 MB committed at 77 SECONDS of uptime** because it booted into post-match state, against 105.6 MB for the same fresh boot with no game played. A fresh boot is therefore NOT reliably ~105 MB, and any future "from-boot baseline" must record whether a match had just ended. This is also why `_LIMIT_MB` is 1200 and not 1000: 805 MB is NORMAL post-game behaviour, so 1000 would have left only ~195 MB of headroom over a routine state. **Two measurement caveats, recorded rather than buried:** (1) the formal 5-minute post-game-2 verdict line NEVER PRINTED - editing `core/resource_manager.py` tripped RC's hot-reload and the pid churned 21348 -> 20260 -> 6692, which correctly ABORTED the ratchet watcher (it is built to refuse a cross-process comparison). The verdict rests on the in-game means and the committed-memory delta, both captured on the single pre-restart process, not on that missing sample. (2) A ~+1.2 MB/min in-game drift is visible but is NOT separable from the 500-548 oscillation - do NOT report it as a finding. **Do NOT walk the constants back without re-measuring**, and do NOT touch the restart-loop guard, which was correct throughout. Original filing and the full from-boot curve below. The clean from-boot measurement the filing asked for was taken (RC restarted 15:02, pid 21348, sampled every 60s under a live dashboard client doing ~1600 req/min, i.e. the same load the aged process carried - the sampler reads the pid from `health.json` each tick so a supervisor restart would be recorded, not silently followed). **Curve:** idle RSS is FLAT for 10 minutes, oscillating 88-147 MB with no trend, nowhere near the ceiling. Game start takes a single **+392 MB STEP** (`t=602s rss 97.5` -> `t=662s rss 489.7`, private 127.4 -> 962.1, threads 19 -> 54). In-game across a full 23-minute ARAM, n=140: **min 499.7 / max 547.6 / mean 518.8**. **So playing a game IS the breach** - RC's normal in-game working set sits just above a 500 MB ceiling, which is why the guard fires at ERROR every 60s for an entire match. Nothing grows without bound. **RAISE THE CEILING; do not hunt a leak, and do not touch the restart-loop guard.** Constants are hardcoded with no env override at `core/resource_manager.py:46-47` (`_WARN_MB = 300`, `_LIMIT_MB = 500`); note the watchdog gates on RSS (`WorkingSet64`), which is the noisier signal - RSS oscillated while private memory climbed monotonically through warm-up. **THE ONE RESIDUAL, and the reason this is not CLOSED: the step does NOT release at match end** (4 min post-game RSS was still 512.6 MB, private 1000.5 MB, not back near 100). That is a ratchet, and it is the plausible route to the 787-810 MB the aged process reached, since the operator played at least twice that day. A slow in-game drift of ~+1.2 MB/min is also present but is NOT separable from the 500-548 oscillation over a single 23-minute window - **do not report that slope as a finding**. **The cheap discriminator is one MORE game on the SAME process:** if RSS lands ~520 again the step is per-game-idempotent and raising the ceiling is the whole fix; if it lands ~900 it is per-game residue and the fix is releasing what the game allocates. Pick the new `_LIMIT_MB` only AFTER that, because a number chosen from one match is wrong if the ratchet is real. Evidence: `scratchpad/rm146_rss.csv` + `scratchpad/g603_log.csv` (session-local, not committed). ORIGINAL FILING BELOW, preserved - its log-derived numbers are consistent with the above and its "do not guess between the two" instruction is what produced this answer. Measured across all four log rotations for 2026-08-02: 50 `Memory limit exceeded` ERRORs spanning 10:12 (`782 MB`) to 14:07 (`559 MB`), never dropping under the limit for long. `MEM-REMEDIATION TRIGGERED` fired twice in the morning (`SrAramWorker restarted` at 10:14:35 and 10:23:46) and since then every trigger is declined: `MEM-REMEDIATION suppressed: rss=515 MB sustained (>= 500 MB x 3 samples) but within cooldown (362s / 600s elapsed) - NOT restarting (restart-loop guard)` (`ops/.../resource_manager.py:166`, limit check at `:233`, trigger at `:194`). **The restart-loop guard is CORRECT and must not be the thing that gets changed** - it is doing exactly its job. The defect is upstream of it: either the 500 MB ceiling is simply wrong for current RC (in which case raising it is the fix and the ERROR-level logging should go with it) or something genuinely leaks and the twice-daily `SrAramWorker` restart is masking it. **Do not guess between those two** - the discriminator is whether RSS grows monotonically from a fresh boot or plateaus, which needs one clean measurement from a restart, not a log read. Secondary harm, and the reason this is filed rather than ignored: it emits at ERROR every 60s into `logs/YYYY-MM-DD.log`, which is the same file the live-gated receipts are read from, and it is a large part of why that log now rotates through 3 MB roughly every 20 minutes. NOT investigated in the filing session (out of scope for RM-145, filed at operator instruction).

- **RM-147 CLOSED 2026-08-02 - decision taken, source added, G6-03 RUN AND CLOSED on it the same session (LEDGER 1170).** The Display Capture was enabled for one live ARAM, recorded 25.08 min across a real match end with zero stalls, and auto-disabled afterward, so OBS is back to its pre-G6-03 state. **Two traps measured while arming it, both cheap to re-hit:** a freshly enabled `monitor_capture` renders a BLANK frame for the first few seconds, so a screenshot taken immediately after `SetSceneItemEnabled` reads as a dead source (994-byte uniform PNG) - settle ~3s before judging; and all three `method` values (0 Auto / 1 DXGI / 2 WGC) render identically once settled (163,780-163,786 byte PNGs), so a blank frame is never evidence about the method. ## 2026-08-02 - RM-145 PRE-FIX DIAGNOSIS (relocated from ROADMAP 2026-08-02)

Relocated VERBATIM once the row shipped AND was live-confirmed (G6-04 CLOSED). Kept because the diagnosis method is the reusable part - the cause was an ABSENCE (no display listener registered at all), found by grep rather than by reading a wrong value.

- **RM-145 ORIGINAL FILING (kept for the trace) - the Electron overlay never recomputes its scale when the display mode changes.** Operator-reported twice via the steer channel 2026-08-02 ("switched to 1920x1080 when the game client switched video modes but it has not reverted despite correcting the in-game video settings back to borderless & 1440"; then "overlay is still at the wrong resolution"). **Traced, not guessed:** `rc-shell/src/main.js` calls `ov.resolveOverlayMetrics({workArea: primary.bounds, ...})` at `:575` and assigns `overlayScale` at `:579` - each exactly ONCE, at window creation - and the file registers **no** `display-metrics-changed` / `display-added` / `display-removed` listener at all (grep is empty). So the scale captured when the overlay window was built is the scale it keeps for the process lifetime, which is precisely the reported symptom: it followed the display DOWN and could not follow it back UP. **Read `docs/OVERLAY_DOCTRINE.md` + the item-567 comment at `main.js:565-574` FIRST** - the choice of `primary.bounds` over the taskbar-excluded work area is load-bearing (work-area sizing makes `ovscale` 1.296 instead of 1.333 and lands every design-px widget ~3 percent off the game minimap), so a fix must RE-RUN that same computation on display change, never substitute a different source. Acceptance: change the display mode with the overlay up and confirm `overlayScale` tracks it in both directions. Restarting rc-shell is the current workaround, not the fix.

## 2026-08-02 - RM-144 vision-not-dead ORIGINAL FILING (relocated from ROADMAP 2026-08-02)

Relocated VERBATIM when ROADMAP.md hit 95 percent of its 81920-byte budget. The row is CLOSED. Kept because the two measurement artifacts it dissects are the reusable part: an `https://` probe against a plain-HTTP token-gated endpoint reads as `http=000 size=0`, and a sticky operator-click dwell field reads as a live outage.

- **RM-144 SHIPPED 2026-08-02 (LEDGER 1165) - vision was NEVER dead; the report was two measurement artifacts stacked, and one of them hid a real bug.** Acceptance met live: `/latest-frame` 200 / 150593 bytes and `screen_read` `{"status":"ok"}`. **Half 1 was a PROBE artifact, not a fault.** The `:8889` relay is plain HTTP and token-gated on `X-RC-Token`; the filed probe used `https://` with no header, so curl reported `http=000 size=0` and that was read as "0 bytes". Probed correctly the frame is fresh every time (`source=self_grab`, 1280x720 jpeg, age 0.1s) - the in-process self-heal in `dashboard/server.py` had been serving frames the whole time. **Half 2 was BY DESIGN on top of a real defect.** `screen_read` is an operator-click-only dwell field (`dashboard/_screen_read.py` -> `data/screen_read.json` -> `_state_builder`), so its `error` was simply the last click, 75.7 days stale. Clicking it live moved `no_fresh_frame` -> `empty_note`, which exposed the actual bug: `GameVisionReader._extract()` prefers `core.moon_proxy.extract_vision(img, model)`, a transport that carries NO prompt, so `vision_server/_inference.py` answers every caller with its fixed TFT schema and `self.PROMPT` is only ever sent on the direct-Anthropic fallback. `ScreenReadVision.PROMPT` asks for `{"note": ...}`, the relay never emits `note`, so SCREEN READ could not return `ok` on any click since it shipped. Fixed with a `USE_RELAY` class flag (default True - mode coaches keep the relay and its dedupe); `ScreenReadVision` sets it False. `core/moon_proxy.py` is frozen and was not touched. New `tests/test_vision_prompt_transport.py` (3 tests, red first) pins both directions. **Do not re-probe `:8889` over `https://`, and do not re-file a stale `screen_read` as a vision outage** - see memories `reference_vision_token_canonical` + `reference_screen_read_sticky_bydesign`.

## 2026-08-02 - RM-145 overlay display-mode tracking ORIGINAL FILING (relocated from ROADMAP 2026-08-02)

Relocated VERBATIM the same day the row was live-confirmed and G6-04 closed, when ROADMAP.md hit 95 percent of its 81920-byte budget. The row is CLOSED. Kept because the `reposition`/`reload` split and the item-567 `primary.bounds` constraint are the reusable part - a future edit must not fix tracking by quietly breaking alignment.

- **RM-145 SHIPPED + LIVE-CONFIRMED 2026-08-02 (LEDGER 1166; G6-04 CLOSED the same day).** In-game receipt on rc-shell pid 4140: desktop 2560x1440 -> 1920x1080 -> 2560x1440 with the overlay window tracking (2560x1440 -> 1920x1080 -> 2560x1440, `vis=True` throughout) and the access log carrying `?overlay=1` (scale 1.00) -> `?overlay=1&ovscale=1.33` in both directions. Two traps recorded on G6-04: Borderless does NOT move the desktop resolution so it fires no event and proves nothing (use exclusive Fullscreen), and a mode switch emits a ~1s bounce at the old scale that must not be read as the result. Original filing text below. `rc-shell/src/main.js` now registers `display-metrics-changed` / `display-added` / `display-removed` (it registered none), coalesces the burst Windows emits during a mode switch on a 600ms settle, and re-runs the SAME `resolveOverlayMetrics({workArea: primary.bounds, ...})` create time runs - item 567's `primary.bounds` source is preserved verbatim and pinned by a test that asserts the re-apply never reads `primary.workArea`. The decision is the pure `ov.resolveOverlayDisplayChange(prev, next)`, which splits `reposition` (setBounds) from `reload` (the `ovscale` URL param is baked in at loadURL, so only a reload moves the renderer's body zoom) - the split exists so a taskbar auto-hide toggle mid-fight does not flash the HUD. 13 tests, red first, incl. a mutation-checked assertion that the registrar is actually called at app ready. **The live half is genuinely gated and was NOT substituted away:** the re-apply needs an overlay WINDOW, which is created lazily on first in-game show, so a headless resolution flip early-returns and proves nothing. See G6-04 for the steps + the `ovscale=N` access-log receipt. Restarting rc-shell remains the workaround until MAIN is relaunched on this code (G6-01).

## 2026-07-29 - RM-125 original filing + RM-126 DONE narrative (relocated verbatim from ROADMAP.md at the 94 pct doc-budget breach)

Both rows are settled: RM-125's filing is explicitly historical and RM-126 is DONE (`65beb575`). Kept verbatim because their measurements are the reason they are worth retaining - the 3153-character non-ASCII census and the two-latch drag fix.

- **RM-125 ORIGINAL FILING (historical, 2026-07-28) - the 7-bit ASCII rule was violated across 31 shipped web files and the commit gate structurally could not see it.** CLAUDE.md's hard rule covers *comments* as authored content, and `web/` carried **3153 non-ASCII characters across 31 `.html` / `.js` / `.css` files** (filed as 3154; the disk re-measure at R222 read 3153). Split, because the two halves needed different treatment: **2884 (91 pct) sat in COMMENT lines** - box-drawing separators U+2500 (2662 alone), U+2192 arrows, U+00A7, U+00B7 - and are mechanically sweepable; **270 sit in LIVE lines** and are NOT, because some are deliberate UI glyphs for the Terminal theme and a blind sweep would change rendered output. Worst files: `web/js/main.js` (1368 comment / 103 live), `web/css/panels/input_activity.css` (223/1), `web/js/panels/right_now.js` (185/31). **Why it survived every gate:** `tools/precommit_gate.py` scans STAGED LINES only, so a glyph sitting in a comment nobody has edited since 2026-05-18 is never in a diff (the same scope limit that let U+00D7 through this morning - now closed for NEW lines by `afcbcf79`, which does nothing for residue already on disk). And `tools/p3_ascii_sweep.py`, the repo's own comment-glyph sweeper, is **`ast`-based and therefore Python-only** - it cannot parse `.js` / `.css` / `.html` at all, so it has never once looked at `web/`. Running it reports `0 substitutions across 0 files` and that reads as clean. **Do NOT sweep this blind.** The 270 live-line characters must be adjudicated per case first; only then is the comment half safe to automate. Needs a non-`ast` comment tokeniser for the three web languages, which is the actual unit of work here. Find residue with a whole-file byte scan, never by trusting the hook's history.

- **RM-126 DONE (filed 2026-07-28 by R223, FIXED 2026-07-28 by R224, commit `65beb575`).** Fixed on the attach side exactly as this row required, with TWO distinct latches because the two hosts have different lifetimes: `_installDrag` now stores its `begin` closure on the element and returns the STORED one on re-entry, and `_makeHandle` latches the ACTIVE-mode body `pointerdown` on `el.dataset.ovxBodyDrag` (the idiom `_makeHideMenu` already used). The latch sits AFTER the handle bind, so the freshly created `.ovx-handle` child keeps rebinding every pass. **Returning the STORED closure is the load-bearing half, not an optimisation** - skipping the binds while handing back a FRESH closure would leave the surviving el-level listeners closed over the first call's drag state, trading a leak for a silent desync. Proven behaviourally, not only by source-parse: a node harness driving three `_makeHandle` passes with the handle child dropped between them measures **12 el-level binds on baseline `08c8aade` (4 per pass, linear) against 4 on the fixed tree**, with the handle rebinding 3 times on both sides. Defect-class enumeration covered all 19 `addEventListener` sites across `overlay_layout.js` + `overlay_idle.js`: 4 FIXED, 15 OUT-OF-SCOPE with reasons, 0 new instances. `_ensureLauncher` was already immune for precisely the reason `_makeHandle` was not - it queries the HOST element itself, not a child. The 16 destructive subtree writes catalogued below were left untouched, as this row required. **Original filing, for the record:** `web/js/lib/overlay_layout.js` leaks pointer listeners on every overlay repaint. `_makeHandle` guards on "does a `.ovx-handle` child already exist" and then calls `_installDrag(el, w)`, which attaches `pointermove` / `pointerup` / `pointercancel` to the PERSISTENT widget element (`:546-549`, called from `:571`). Every renderer that rebuilds its mount with `innerHTML` destroys the handle child, so the next `_placeAll` re-runs `_installDrag` and adds 3 more listeners to the same element, which never goes away. The rebuild pattern is contract, not a defect - `:932-948` documents and compensates for it - so the fix belongs on the attach side (attach once per element, or tear down before re-attaching), NOT in a rewrite of 7 panels. **Blast radius measured, not guessed:** 16 destructive subtree writes across 7 files (`callouts.js` 118/129/139/148, `coach_choices.js` 201/213, `enemy_spells.js` 120/199, `next_buy.js` 95/104, `objective_gauges.js` 275/284, `spike_cue.js` 86/125, `stats_panel.js` 170/332) - once per repaint per widget for the life of an overlay session. Tier-1, no engine, no schema. Not shipped in R223 because it is a cross-file owner change and that slice owned `callouts.*` only.

## 2026-07-26 - R194 DS vamp/sustain follow-ons (RM-116 CLOSED, ENGINE 1.256.0)

### The row that did not survive contact with arithmetic

RM-116 (b) asked for Sundered Sky 6610's overheal-to-bonus-health, "Meraki-cited and
UNMODELLED", modelled on Bloodthirster's `ItemShield` shape. The Meraki clause is real -
`items_meraki.json` item 6610 "Lightshield Strike" ends `Excess healing beyond
{{as|'''maximum''' health}} is converted to {{as|'''bonus''' health}} for 8 seconds.` -
which is exactly why the row was persuasive. The model is still wrong, on two independent
grounds:

1. **It double counts.** `compute_ehp` puts `heal_total` and `shield_any_amped` in the SAME
   EHP numerator across all three of `physical_ehp` / `magical_ehp` / `true_ehp`, and
   `_collect_heals` credits `ItemHeal.resolve_magnitude` in FULL - the only adjustments are
   takedown gating and a non-positive skip, with no clamp against missing HP. The engine
   therefore ALREADY assumes zero healing is wasted, which is precisely the guarantee the
   overheal conversion provides. Measured with the naive shield injected: Aatrox L11
   physical EHP 3991.0 -> 4348.2, all 357.2 (+8.9%) of it double count.
2. **The honest form is identically zero.** The correct term is
   `max(0, heal_magnitude - missing_hp)`. Under the shipped
   `_MISSING_HP_SHARE_FOR_HEALS = 0.5` (`ehp.py:357`, consumed at `ehp.py:1645`), the
   per-trigger heal is `base_ad + 0.06 * missing_hp`. Swept over all 173 champions at L1 and
   L18, the worst heal-to-missing ratio is **0.2205 (Kled L1)**; the clamp would require
   `base_ad >= 0.47 * max_hp`, which no champion approaches. A DEFAULT-OFF seam that
   resolves to 0.0 even when armed is not a model.

**Why Bloodthirster's shape does not transfer:** Ichorshield accrues from LIFESTEAL, which
ticks on minions and camps out of combat at full HP - a genuine pre-fight accrual lane
disjoint from the in-fight heal pool, and the stated basis for its full-cap steady-state
assumption. Sundered Sky fires only off the next basic attack against a champion, so its
heal and its overheal are one trigger, mutually exclusive by construction. Pinned by
`test_sundered_sky_overheal_refute_r194.py` (12 tests), including a census asserting no item
carries both an `ItemHeal` and an `ItemShield`.

### The sweep that narrowed instead of widening

RM-116 (c) is real and shipped, but the obvious implementation was wrong. Meraki states the
Ravenous Cleave passive and the Ravenous Crescent active both benefit from life steal at
100% effectiveness, and the naive read is that the `hydra_cleave` family does. It does not:
**Tiamat 3077, Titanic Hydra 3748, Profane Hydra 6698 and Stridebreaker 6631 all ship the
identical Cleave shape with NO lifesteal sentence**, so a name-based or family-key fold
would have silently over-credited four items. The eligible set resolves by ID SUFFIX to
exactly `{"3074", "223074"}`. A naive substring grep for "lifesteal" false-positives on all
five items via the `"lifesteal": {"flat": 0.0}` stat key - the clause lives in the `effects`
prose field, and that is where the check has to look.

No coefficient was invented: the Cleave magnitude is read back out of the item's own
`PeriodicProc.bonus_damage` against a `CallContext`, the Crescent out of its own
`physical_burst_total_ad_ratio`, routed through `collect_effects` so `hydra_cleave`
first-seen-wins is honoured. DEFAULT-OFF is guaranteed by the FLAG rather than the target
count, because Cleave contributes nothing at `targets_in_rotation=1.0` but Crescent does.

### The seam that was stranded one lane short

RM-116 (a): `assume_max_stacks_omnivamp` had been reachable on `/ehp` since R193 slice C but
could never influence a RANKING, which is the surface every generated build table and live
coach tick actually reads. It now reaches `rank_items_by_ehp` behind `score_by="sustain"`.
The seam is NOT the RM-115 inert shape - a uniform multiplier on the EHP numerator is
invariant under a ratio sort key, but `_blend_with_heal` folds the vamp pool in as an
ADDEND and only candidates carrying omnivamp earn one. Measured on Amumu L13 SR behind
Sunfire Aegis 3068 + Plated Steelcaps 3047 over the full 138-item pool: Riftmaker 4633 moves
blended rank 43 -> sustain rank 35 (`delta_ehp` 734.1252302631583 vs `delta_sustain_ehp`
849.3574186147398) while Rylai's 3116 sits 35 -> 36 at the identity 839.0002631578955 on
both. OFF is bit-identical: 2827 rows over 22 champion/mode cases, max absolute deviation
exactly 0.0, zero order mismatches.

`/rank-tank` is the ONLY EHP-family ranker route, so no sibling is left stranded:
`/rank-bruiser` ranks on `rank_items_by_hybrid`, and `hybrid.py` carries no
`effective_ehp_with_sustain` surface at all.

### RM-01 Lane E - the fusion shadow ledger accrued, and it exposed a defect

Re-probed 2026-07-25 - the 2026-07-18 "file does not exist" note is STALE. `data/fusion_shadow.jsonl` holds **230 real-game records**; the accrual gate is MET. Triaged same day: **41 of 41 CV overrides in the ledger's entire history were garbage** - all `gold`, all the literal value `1`, against anchors of 913 / 8703 / 6423 / 12761 / 30410. TWO causes: `core/vision_routing.py:118` merges any key the Sonnet escalation returns unfiltered by the requested field list (the relay answers a TFT-shaped prompt in all modes), and `core/vision_fusion.py` had NO plausibility check so the unconditional 0.7 CV heuristic always cleared the 0.6 stale-override threshold. FIXED at the fusion layer (plausibility gate; ledger replay moves exactly 41 decisions, all gold, `lc_exact` + `cv_fallback` untouched). Tesseract is NOT the culprit - `gold == 1` appears in only 3 of 2129 `ocr_shadow.jsonl` rows. **`vision_routing.py:118` is the un-fixed upstream half** - deliberately deferred, it changes served coach dicts. Still shadow-only; do NOT flip.

Additional measurements from the triage: 230 records spanning 2026-07-18 to 2026-07-24, 0 unparseable; `live_stale` 56 true / 174 false; 2165 total field-decisions splitting `lc_exact` 692 / `cv_fallback` 1305 / `lc_stale` 127 / `cv_override_stale` 41. The 41 overrides are the entire population of contested decisions the layer has ever made, and all 41 were wrong. LC anchors overridden: 913 (x17), 8703 (x10), 6423 (x9), 87 (x3), 12761, 30410. All 59 `gold: 1` records share a degenerate `cv_reads` shape of exactly `{"gold": 1}` - one key, no `timer` canary - versus 13-16 fields in every healthy record. A REJECTED rule worth recording: monotonic-decreasing gold is NOT a valid invariant, because League `currentGold` legitimately drops on every purchase; the shipped gate uses monotonic-non-decreasing for `level`/`cs` only, plus a 10x divergence test above an absolute floor of 50, which is what actually catches all 41.

## 2026-07-24 - RM-41 burst off-class exclusion full narrative (relocated from ROADMAP)

- **RM-41 SHIPPED 2026-07-24 (ENGINE 1.240.0, DEFAULT-OFF `exclude_off_axis_items`).** `ds.burst` is axis-agnostic by design - it serves AD assassins on lethality AND AP assassins on burst magic - but it ranked every purchasable, mode-legal candidate by raw burst delta with no notion of which axis the kit actually scales on, so AD spellblade / on-hit / crit procs got credited on an AP assassin's ability-EMPOWERED AUTO. **Defect re-confirmed live at 1.239.0 before any code was written** (the sweep's original probe was at 1.216.0): against the sweep-standard squishy target (armor 30 / mr 30 / hp 1900 / bonus 800, L13, empty build) Akali - 85.5 percent magical damage, an assassin who buys zero AD in any source - was served Essence Reaver #4, Trinity Force #5, Blade of The Ruined King #7 and Infinity Edge #12, with Hextech Gunblade buried at #11 beneath all four. The mirror direction is the RM-35 note (dead AP items in an AD burst champ's list), so the seam was built SYMMETRIC and one flag covers both; **RM-35's own crit-burst cohort work is untouched.**
  - **NEW `agents/daemon_slayer/_burst_off_axis.py`**, applied at the `_filter_candidates` seam in `burst.rank_items_by_burst` and route-surfaced on `/rank-assassin`. **Neither gate is a curated list, which is the property to preserve.** (1) The CHAMPION gate reads `lolmath.damage_distribution` off the snapshot's own record at the same dominance / margin thresholds as `core.archetype_picks._axis_from_distribution` (0.55 / 0.20), held as local literals because the DS package does not import `core` in production; a test pins both resolvers to the same verdict on the AP cohort and the AD fence set. A champion without a decisive split is a NO-OP. (2) The ITEM gate keys on three DDragon offensive stat fields only - `FlatPhysicalDamageMod` / `FlatCritChanceMod` versus `FlatMagicDamageMod` - and strips only when the item carries offense on the OFF axis and NONE on the ON axis.
  - **Two deliberate tightenings, both of which contradict the original spec and are the reason to read this entry before touching the seam.** The spec prescribed a hand-curated deny list naming nine items including Statikk Shiv; the shipped rule is data-driven instead, and **Statikk Shiv correctly SURVIVES** because at 16.14.1 it carries 45 AP alongside 45 AD - it is a genuine hybrid, not pollution. Hextech Gunblade (80 AP + 40 AD) survives by the same construction, which is what the spec wanted and had to special-case. Separately, **attack speed is deliberately NOT treated as a physical-offense signal**: it is on-axis for AP on-hit kits (Nashor's, Guinsoo's) and crediting it would drag Berserker's Greaves into a strip this seam is not meant to make. Every defensive / utility item and every boot carries offense on neither axis and is untouched on both.
  - **MEASURED flag-ON, L13 vs the squishy target.** The seven-champion `_AP_ASSASSIN_IDS` cohort drops 140 candidates to 88 and **6 of 7 change their top-8**: Akali loses Essence Reaver / Trinity / BotRK and Gunblade climbs #11 -> #8. **Leblanc's top-8 is BYTE-IDENTICAL**, which independently reproduces the sweep's finding that her kit has no empowered-auto hook for AD procs to ride - a prediction the sweep made in 2026-07 and the build confirmed without being told to look for it. On the AD side Zed drops 140 to 102 with a **byte-identical top-8**: his lethality core is untouched and only dead AP rows leave. Shaco (0.521 magical / 0.347 physical - dominant but inside the margin) is a NO-OP at 140.
  - **Byte-identity at the default is PROVEN, not asserted:** all 9 regenerated build-order tables differ in `engine_version` + `generated_at` only, zero content lines. The seam is a candidate STRIP and never a reweight - a test pins that the surviving rows keep their relative model order. `agents/daemon_slayer/tests/test_burst_off_axis_rm41.py` (19 cases) covers axis-gate verdicts, the item predicate in both directions, hybrid + utility survival, default byte-identity, a CHARACTERIZATION of the defect at the default so a future refactor cannot silently "fix" it, cohort strip, the Gunblade climb, AD-fence retention, the indecisive no-op, order preservation, and two live-route cases. **Default-ON flip is gated row `G2-43`** - a strip is invisible in the UI (the item simply is not there), so a wrong exclusion cannot be caught by looking at what IS shown.

## 2026-07-20 - RM-100 / RM-106 / RM-106a / RM-106b full narratives (relocated from ROADMAP)

- **RM-100 ops: the nightly critic + the nightly suite were both silently dead; repaired 2026-07-19 (gemini-loop cycle 1, R130/R131; `aa90e9b4` / `fb88c7d8` / `cf71753f`).** Two independent silent-failure classes, both invisible to the surfaces we actually watch. (a) **RC-GeminiAudit produced nothing for 28 nights while reading Enabled/Ready.** `ops/runtime/gemini_last_audit.txt` pinned a worktree-slice sha that never survived cherry-pick, so `git log <dangling>..HEAD` came back empty and `tools/gemini_audit.ps1` took its own "nothing to audit" branch and exited 0 without writing a review OR a log line - `logs/gemini_audit.log` did not exist at all. Now self-heals to `HEAD~10` with a loud WARN and logs `START` unconditionally as its first write. The separate `0xC000013A` last-run result is **UNPROVEN and still open** - six hypotheses refuted with evidence (TTY/stdin, InteractiveToken teardown, the marker itself, oversized stdin, missing `-NoProfile`, logoff kill), so the task was deliberately NOT re-registered; the new START line makes the next occurrence attributable (START then silence = killed mid-run; no START = died before line 20). **If 0xC000013A recurs on a later nightly, the marker fix is not the cause - read the log.** (b) **The nightly full-suite had been red for 12 consecutive days** (runs 28935372989 .. 29682372934) and nobody saw it, because the push `check` job is green BY CONSTRUCTION - it never runs `tests/` as one process, so it cannot reproduce the pollution. Fixed test-side only: Playwright's session-scoped ProactorEventLoop leaves asyncio's per-thread running-loop marker set on the main thread, breaking any later bare `asyncio.run()`; and the Jhin build-order test depended on a live `:8893` that CI can never spawn (`creationflags=0x08000000` raises on Linux). **Latent, unfixed:** `tests/snapshot_panels` still leaks that marker, so any NEW test calling bare `asyncio.run()` on the main thread and sorting after it will fail identically - use the `_run_coro` / `_run_poll_loop` pattern (now 5 near-identical local copies; consolidating them is the open follow-up). **MECHANISM CORRECTED 2026-07-20 (measured on Legion, py3.14 + playwright 1.59.0) - the earlier "playwright never clears the marker, it stays set for the rest of the session" phrasing is WRONG and made the bug read as unfixable from the test side.** What actually happens: `playwright/_impl/_sync_base.py:114` (and the identical site at `:56`) calls `asyncio._set_running_loop(self._loop)` after every sync call and never pairs it with a `_set_running_loop(None)` - but `PlaywrightContextManager.__exit__` (`playwright/sync_api/_context_manager.py:86-98`) calls `stop_sync()` -> `_connection.py:319` `loop.run_until_complete(...)`, and `run_until_complete`'s own `finally` restores the marker to `None`. So exit DOES clear it, as a side effect, and **the leak is BOUNDED BY THE CONTEXT MANAGER, not permanent**; it persists across the session only because the `pw_browser` fixture is `scope="session"` (`tests/snapshot_panels/conftest.py:246`). Probe: marker before start = `None`; inside the session after `page.set_content()` = `<ProactorEventLoop running=True closed=False>`; a bare run inside the session = RuntimeError "asyncio.run() cannot be called from a running event loop"; marker after `cm.__exit__()` = `None`; a bare run after exit = ok. **Recorded as a TRADEOFF, not a recommendation:** narrowing `pw_browser` off session scope WOULD bound the leak, but costs a browser launch across ~387 snapshot_panels tests - a real cost, not a free fix. Zero bare `asyncio.run(` calls currently remain under `tests/`, so the latent bug has no live trigger today, and a guard test now pins that. The bug remains LATENT - nothing here is a shipped fix. _Id note: this took RM-100, not RM-99 - `docs/DS_SWEEP_TRACKER.md` has RM-99 explicitly reserved as the next free DS GAP id, and an explicit reservation outranks closing the numbering hole._
- **RM-106 SHIPPED 2026-07-19 - the sanctioned pull is BUILT, LIVE-PROVEN, and on the 15-minute schedule.** `tools/rofl_archiver.py --pull` now runs the Match-V5 `/replays` route (`core/rofl_archive.download_replays` + `core/riot_api.get_replay_urls`), resolving each account's PUUID fresh by Riot ID. Measured on the live run: **5 replays downloaded and archived for SamplePlayer#Trist**, and a second run skipped all 5 (idempotent). **FOUR things were only learnable by running it, all now encoded in tests:** (1) the bodies arrive **GZIP-framed**, and urllib does not decompress - the first live pull discarded 5 of 5 as "not a replay" until `_maybe_gunzip` landed; (2) **SamplePlayer#Vayne's five URLs all 404** - Riot LISTS the match but no longer retains the file, which is permanent and expected, so it is counted `gone` and does NOT fail the scheduled run (otherwise `LastTaskResult=1` forever); (3) the two sources spell one match differently (`NA1-x.rofl` from the client, `NA1_x.rofl` from the API), so a filename-keyed skip re-downloads 10 MB - the check is now match-id-keyed across both forms; (4) an S3 body that is not a replay is discarded rather than written, which is what caught (1) instead of poisoning the archive. **The cache defect below is FIXED:** `account:v1:` cache keys now carry a truncated-sha256 fingerprint of the active API key, so a key rotation naturally misses and re-resolves (`test_key_rotation_invalidates_the_account_cache`). **OPERATOR HYPOTHESIS - STILL OPEN, now instrumented rather than guessed:** every pull appends what it saw to `<archive>/pull_log.jsonl`, and `--pull` prints a rotation verdict. Four observations so far, all with NO games played in between, so `rotated=False` proves nothing yet; `pull_rotation_report` deliberately returns `rotated=None` on a single observation rather than fabricating a negative. **Play games, then run `--pull` and read the rotation line** - if the window rotates, the 15-minute cadence already converts it into a permanent archive and no bulk trick is needed. Original measurement record follows. **SUPERSEDED - Riot serves `.rofl` files directly, sanctioned, with an ordinary API key. MEASURED 2026-07-19.** `GET https://americas.api.riotgames.com/lol/match/v5/matches/by-puuid/{puuid}/replays` -> **HTTP 200** `{"total": 5, "matchFileURLs": [...]}`, each a PRE-SIGNED S3 URL on `lol-prod-us-west-2-match-history-replay` with `response-content-disposition=attachment; filename="NA1_xxxx.rofl"`. No third party, no bearer-token scraping, no `.bat`. **Bounds: `X-Amz-Expires=3600` (1 hour) and exactly 5 per account** - a refreshing recency window, not an archive, which is why it PAIRS with `tools/rofl_archiver.py` (pull 5 -> archive permanently -> extract) rather than replacing it. **THE TRAP THAT COST AN HOUR - PUUIDs ARE ENCRYPTED PER API KEY.** Cycling the key invalidates every stored PUUID; all three of ours returned `400 "Bad Request - Exception decrypting <puuid>"`. Worse, `core/riot_api.get_account_by_riot_id` checks `get_cache().get_immutable()` BEFORE any network call (`riot_api.py:346`), so a "re-resolve" silently returns the OLD key's cached PUUID and the 400 persists. Bypassing the cache produced NEW puuid strings and immediate 200s. **CONSEQUENCE, unfixed: every PUUID in `rewind_history.db` (2961 matches) is stale against the API** - still valid as an internal join key, useless as a request parameter - and NOTHING invalidates the immutable cache on key rotation. Fix both before any bulk pull. **ENTITLEMENT, confirmed on the developer portal (app 834837 "Riot Commander"):** `/replays` is an EXPLICITLY APPROVED endpoint of the PRODUCT app, not an undocumented backdoor - which is why the same request 400s with the personal/dev key and 200s with the product key. `API-Key-Riot.txt` must hold the PRODUCT key. Rate limit **20000/10s** (vs 2000/10s on the core Match-V5 routes), so the pull is NOT throughput-constrained - the binding limits are the 5-per-account cap and the 1-hour URL expiry. Do not build backoff for a limit that will never bind. That probe ran while `EnableReplayApi` was ABSENT; it measured the flag-OFF state and was WRONG. **TWO REAL LIMITS (measured, not assumed):** `/liveclientdata/activeplayerabilities` returns **HTTP 400** in a replay (no active player in a spectator context), so **SKILL ORDER is NOT recoverable**; and `eventdata` at t=600 carried only `GameStart` / `ChampionKill` / `Multikill` with NO `ITEM_PURCHASED`, so items come from SAMPLING, never from the event stream. **HARD BOUND AMENDED 2026-07-19 (same session) - the "forward-capture only, cannot backfill" line is CONDITIONALLY FALSE and must NOT be re-inherited as written.** It rested on two premises that both failed within the hour: that no old `.rofl` could be obtained, and that no matching old client existed. Measured: a third-party service HOSTS `.rofl` files on its own servers (`GET /lol/download-rofl/{match_id}` plus a short-lived `Authorization: Bearer` JWT carrying `match_id` + `owner`), which delivered a real 10353126-byte `NA1_5595187452.rofl` on patch 16.13 that `core.rofl_archive.extract_stats` parsed cleanly at 18 players x 367 fields; and patch-specific game files are separately obtainable, so its launcher pairs the downloaded `.rofl` with a matching OLD client. **CONSEQUENCE: seek-and-sample CAN backfill history** - any archived match, for any patch a client is kept for, yields per-timestamp item / gold / level state over the same `:2999` route proven above. The limit is that archive's DEPTH plus how many old clients are installed locally, NOT Riot retention. **Still true, unchanged:** Riot's OWN endpoint serves nothing historical (a 16.13 match measured `incompatible` against a 16.14 client), the capture is interactive and NEVER a background job, and `EnableReplayApi=1` must also be set in the OLD client's `game.cfg`. **NOT MEASURED - do not assume:** how far back that archive reaches; test the older ids before planning any bulk backfill. > **CITATION CAVEAT (measured 2026-07-18) - about half the commit hashes cited for
> 2026-04 through 2026-06 do NOT resolve in this repo. This is a known, bounded,
> already-self-corrected defect. Do not chase them.**
>
> Measured across `docs/history_notes.md` + `docs/LEDGER.md` + `docs/ROADMAP_HISTORY.md`:
> 387 of 1148 distinct 8-hex citations (34 percent) fail `git rev-parse --verify`.
> They are NOT scattered rot and NOT a history rewrite - a rewrite would be 100 percent
> before a cutoff and 0 percent after. The real distribution is a steady rate that
> stops dead:
>
> | month | resolvable | missing | miss rate |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | 2026-04 | 1 | 3 | 75% |
> | 2026-05 | 53 | 48 | 47% |
> | 2026-06 | 452 | 457 | 50% |
> | 2026-07 | 537 | 0 | **0%** |
>
> **Cause:** the orchestrator workflow (worktree build agents, one merger) had agents
> commit inside their own worktree, and the merger cherry-picked the result. Entries
> then cited BOTH hashes - e.g. "merge `91b6b847` (slice `03927664`, worktree agent)".
> The merge hash entered `main` and resolves; the slice hash never did and never will.
> `git rev-list --all` equals `HEAD` (3645), so the slice objects are not hiding on
> another ref or in the reflog - they are gone.
>
> **The work still landed.** A dead slice hash does not mean the change is missing; it
> means that entry cited the pre-cherry-pick hash. Verify by the MERGE hash, the file,
> or the test - never by the slice hash.
>
> **Already fixed going forward:** 0 of 537 citations dated 2026-07 are unresolvable, so
> the convention corrected itself. No process change is needed.
>
> **Deliberately NOT repaired in place.** The correct hashes are unrecoverable, and
> rewriting 387 historical citations would violate the append-only rule these files run
> on. This note is additive. It exists because the defect has already cost real work:
> a 2026-07-18 audit spent a full agent trying to resolve `541cd9d3` to disambiguate a
> live-gated row, and that hash is simply gone.

## Shipped/closed - relocated from Open items - Medium priority

- [x] **DS review + augments - bonus-AD-zeroing augment: VERIFIED not an RC bug (2026-05-17 - do not re-investigate).** External report (different League project): an Arena augment ("Adapt") zeroes bonus AD -> Maw shield / Endless Hunger haste / Death's Dance heal floor out; reporter hedged it might be a modeling-accuracy nit. **Confirmed against `effects.py`:** RC models all three as `defensive_only` / **non-DPS** - Maw `3156` (lifeline magic shield, no DPS), Death's Dance `6333` (bleed, no DPS proc), Endless Hunger `2517`+`222517` (Famine bonus-AD->haste + Feast omnivamp explicitly tagged *"utility; no DPS contribution"*). They contribute **zero** to DPS ranking regardless of bonus AD, so a bonus-AD-zeroing augment cannot make DS over- or under-rank them - there is no bonus-AD-scaled credit to distort. The one lifeline-family item RC *does* credit with DPS, Sterak's Gage `3053` "Claws that Catch", is correctly keyed off **base AD** (`bonus_ad_pct_base_ad=0.45`), not bonus AD - also immune. EHP path likewise gives no credit: shield throughput is an explicit Phase-1.5 deferral in `ehp.py` (lifeline family handled only as a dead-unique dedup, never bonus-AD-scaled EHP). **The other project's diagnosis does not lift to RC.** The real, *separate* gap is the already-tracked Phase-1.5 shield/heal throughput + P1b Arena-augment `as_pct` overlay (CLAUDE #26c) - RC currently gives no Arena pick-credit for these defensive items at all, a deliberate modeling boundary, not a bonus-AD over-rank bug.

## 2026-07-19 - RM-99 / R137 Heartsteel permanent-HP half (relocated from ROADMAP.md)

_Relocated verbatim when ROADMAP.md crossed its 81920-byte CI budget. SHIPPED at ENGINE 1.226.0; RM-99b (the damage half's wrong 3.5s cadence) was deliberately NOT relocated - it is still OPEN in ROADMAP.md._

- **RM-99 SHIPPED 2026-07-19 (R137, ENGINE 1.226.0) - DEFAULT-OFF `assume_item_health_stacks`.**
  See the R137 sub-bullet at the end of this item for what shipped and for THREE spec errors in
  the research narrative below (the 8% coefficient is WRONG, the fold site is under-specified, and
  the prescribed R46 plumbing is route-unreachable). Original filing, corrections inline:
  **Heartsteel 3084 permanent-HP half is pinned at ZERO stacks, forever.** Meraki
  "Colossal Consumption" grants permanent bonus health equal to 8% of the empowered proc damage
  (30s cooldown per target). Only the damage half is modelled; `_effects_data.py` disclaims the
  rest verbatim in-line - "The HP-on-damage permanent stack (8% of damage as max HP) is not
  modeled - that's stat-side, not proc-side". No registry credits it. The structural reason is
  the familiar one: `_passive_health_overrides.passive_health_stack_hp` (R46) is EXACTLY this
  axis but is keyed by `(champion_id, ability_key, form_index)`, so an item can never match it,
  and the two item-side HP-numerator lanes that do exist (`_item_mana_health` R105,
  `_item_bonus_hp_amp` R107) are both exact conversions of an already-resolved stat and cannot
  express `procs x hp_per_proc`. Measured live on Sion L13 `[3047, 3068]` via `/rank-tank`:
  Heartsteel sits #3 (2016.80 delta EHP) behind Randuin's 2731.28 and Warmog's 2240.88, each
  proc is worth ~43 EHP, so ~5.2 procs passes Warmog's and ~16.5 takes #1 - ordinary mid-game
  numbers for the item whose entire identity is its stack counter. **Not RM-91** (that is
  HP-not-priced-as-damage and needs an objective change; this is a pure max-HP pool add landing
  inside `ds.ehp`'s existing objective) and **not RM-94** (Mejai's is pinned at MAX stacks, this
  at ZERO). Fix shape: `_item_health_stack.py` + DEFAULT-OFF `assume_item_health_stacks`, folded
  next to `item_bonus_hp_amp_hp`, with a monotone assumed-procs-by-level curve copying the
  stack-count-proxy rationale already written in `_passive_health_overrides.py`. S/M, no schema
  lift. Secondary, offense-side: `every_n_seconds=3.5` drops Meraki's explicit 30s-per-target
  cooldown, so a single-target rotation gets ~8.57x the real proc count - the same proxy number
  serves both.
  - **R137 SHIPPED 2026-07-19 (ENGINE 1.226.0): `_item_health_stack.py` + DEFAULT-OFF
    `assume_item_health_stacks`, folded into the three main per-type EHP numerators.** Registered
    3084 AND the Arena mirror 223084 (which the filing above omits entirely). Route-surfaced on
    `/ehp`, `/rank-tank`, `/hybrid`, `/rank-bruiser`. DS suite 8787 passed / 1 skipped / 2461
    subtests. **THREE ERRORS IN THE PARAGRAPH ABOVE - do not inherit them.** (1) **The coefficient
    is 10%, not 8%.** `items_meraki.json` is FROZEN, not lagging: its body is byte-identical across
    all five vendored patch dirs (md5 `5f2ab2ca072637d9`, 16.10.1 .. 16.14.1) despite five separate
    fetches - the item-side instance of the RM-81 Meraki-pin defect. DDragon `items.json` in the
    SAME patch dir, CommunityDragon 16.14 and the wiki all read 10%, and the wiki's dated `V26.11`
    entry ("increased to 10% from 8%") predicts the exact 8 -> 10 flip observed between the vendored
    16.10.1 and 16.11.1 dirs. Meraki's 8% was correct for V25.04 .. V26.10. Its 30s per-target
    cooldown is still correct - only the coefficient moved. (2) **"folded next to
    `item_bonus_hp_amp_hp`" is under-specified** - there are TWO numerator regions, and this term
    joins the PERMANENT-HP family (`passive_health_hp` / `rune_perm_hp`), which the
    `_blend_with_heal` mirror does not carry, so it is folded into the main block ONLY. (3)
    **"copying the R46 rationale" is right for the MATH and wrong for the PLUMBING** -
    `assume_passive_health_stacks` never reaches `rank_items_by_ehp`, `hybrid.py` or `server.py`,
    so mirroring it would have shipped a lane unreachable from the scorer (same defect as
    `assume_kaenic_shield` / `assume_hsp_amp` / `assume_eclipse_shield` / `assume_chainlaced_shield`
    - that population is LARGER than the RM-104 note claims). R107/R136 plumbing was used instead.
    **DDragon's "(0s) per target" is a proven template artifact**, not a real cooldown: 23 items in
    16.14.1 render `(0s)` and exactly one renders a nonzero value, and Meraki supplies real
    cooldowns for four of the cohort. **The assumed-procs curve is the one judgement in the lane** -

      returning `(status, json)`; `_lcu_get` KEEPS its None-on-failure contract because seven

  has no Vitality passive at all.** Verified against the raw index: base `3083` carries "Warmog's

  Warmog's Heart regen and 4% move speed. This is not a wrong magnitude like R133 - it credits an
  effect the item does not have. Same "base nominal" seeding root cause as R133, different
  registry. S, value-only.

### RM-103

- **RM-103 Unending Despair 2502 self-heal half is uncredited AND mislabelled.** Meraki "Anguish":
  sap nearby champions every 4s for 3% bonus health magic damage AND "heal yourself equal to 250%
  of the post-mitigation damage dealt". `_effects_data.py` models the damage and calls the rest
  "ally self-heal component utility-only" - wrong on both counts (it is a SELF heal, and it is a
  2.5x multiplier per champion hit, not utility). `heal_total` lands in the EHP NUMERATOR of all
  three per-type denominators, so it is resist-amplified. Counterfactual measured at the most
  conservative setting (1 champ in range, 1 trigger per fight window): UD moves #6-8 -> #4 on
  Sion / Ornn / Zac / Leona / Malphite / Sejuani. Fix shape: `_item_proc_heal.py` sibling of
  `_item_omnivamp.py`, folded into `heal_item_total` behind DEFAULT-OFF `assume_item_proc_heal`.
  S, **no schema lift** - `ItemHeal.bonus_hp_scaling` already exists and already resolves, it
  simply has ZERO carriers today (all four `ItemHeal(` entries are AD-scaled).

### RM-105

- **RM-105 `effective_ehp_with_sustain` silently understates whenever ANY permanent-HP-family flag
  is ON - measured 2026-07-19 during the R137 build, pre-existing, NOT a DS-sweep GAP id.**
  `ehp.py` assembles its per-type numerators TWICE: the main block, and the `_blend_with_heal`
  mirror that produces `effective_ehp_with_sustain`. The mirror carries `ext_flat_hp` +
  `item_mana_health_hp` + `item_bonus_hp_amp_hp` + `flat_mit_*` but OMITS the entire PERMANENT-HP
  family - `passive_health_hp` (R46), `rune_perm_hp` (R136) and now `item_health_stack_hp` (R137).
  So the two fields diverge by exactly the omitted HP the moment any of those seams is armed.
  Measured live on Sion L13 `[3084, 3068]`: `apply_rune_health_grants` ON gives blended 6283.41 vs
  sustain 5665.08 (**-618.33**, ~10 percent); `assume_passive_health_stacks` ON gives -301.42;
  `assume_item_health_stacks` ON gives -373.24; at defaults the delta is exactly 0.0000.
  **Nothing catches it:** `test_ehp_sustain_contract.py`'s
  `test_effective_equals_blended_when_no_spellvamp_omnivamp` asserts the equality only at DEFAULT
  flags, and the mirror's own comment claims it mirrors the main numerators - which was true when
  written and stopped being true at R46. **This bites exactly when the standing plan executes:**
  every one of these seams is queued for an operator-gated default-ON flip, and the flip is what
  arms the divergence. Fix shape: add the three terms to `_blend_with_heal` and widen the contract
  test to assert the equality with each seam ARMED, not just at defaults. S, no schema lift. R137
  deliberately followed the family precedent (main-only) rather than widening the divergence with a
  fourth term - correcting the family is this item, not that one.

### RM-16 item 215 (poller relay-first watch) - REFUTED, no code changed

The filed defect ("a dead RC-LiveClientRelay 404 short-circuits 'no game'") does not
reproduce on the 1-PC topology. The relay cannot emit a 404 for a running local game:

- `game_reader/poller.py:70-103` `_try_relay()` sets `_relay_says_no_game = True` only
  on `HTTPError` 404 (`:99-100`). A STALE snapshot returns `None` without the flag
  (`:90-92`); an unreachable relay likewise returns `None` without the flag (`:102-103`).
- `game_reader/poller.py:149-152` short-circuits ONLY on that flag; both other cases
  fall through to direct `:2999` at `:154`. So the flag is the single gate, as filed.
- `vision_server/_http.py:90-99` 404s only when `lc.get("data")` is falsy, and
  `vision_server/_relay.py:187-198` self-reads Riot's `:2999` IN-PROCESS first whenever
  `GAME_HOST` is local and the snapshot is older than `_SELF_READ_STALE_S = 2.0`
  (`_maybe_self_read`, `:138-155`; the read itself at `:113-125`).

So a 404 is emitted only AFTER the vision server has just tried a direct local `:2999`
read and come up empty. That is a genuine "no game", not a dead-agent artifact. The
relay agent being dead changes nothing - `handle_upload_liveclient` (`_relay.py:158`)
only pre-warms the cache. The self-read throttle (`_SELF_READ_MIN_INTERVAL_S = 1.5`,
`_relay.py:106`) cannot starve the poller either: `core/liveclient_cache.py:35-37` polls
at 0.5s, so with the agent dead the cache re-reads `:2999` about every 2.5s and never
crosses into a false 404 while a game is live. The only branch with the self-heal off is
a REMOTE `RC_GAME_HOST` (`_relay.py:192`), where the proposed "prefer direct local
:2999" fix would be useless anyway because Riot binds `:2999` localhost-only on the
remote box (documented `_relay.py:16-20`).

Already pinned by `tests/test_liveclient_self_heal_1pc.py` -
`test_stale_cache_self_reads_2999` (:50), `test_self_read_failure_returns_empty` (:57),
`test_remote_host_no_self_read` (:69). Ran that file plus
`tests/test_liveclient_cache_listeners.py` and
`tests/test_liveclient_cache_reuse_hot02.py`: **19 passed, 0 failed** (0.48s).

STILL OPEN from the same RM-16 bullet: the OBS DXGI match-end capture watch. Only the
poller clause is struck.

### RM-16 item 212 (`_csvMaybePushBuildsToLCU` 4-set cap) - REFUTED, no code changed

RC never evicts a foreign (user-authored) item set. `tools/lcu_agent.py` is the ONLY
writer of `/lol-item-sets/v1/item-sets/{sid}/sets` in the repo, and all three write
handlers are scoped to the `RC-` uid prefix:

- `apply_item_sets_batch` (`tools/lcu_agent.py:1087`):
  `sets = [s for s in sets if str(s.get("uid", "")) not in new_uids]`, where `new_uids`
  (`:1076`) is built exclusively from the batch's OWN `set_uid` values, minted by
  `web/js/panels/champ_select.js:2341` as `RC-<champion>-<mode>-<uidKey>`. Only an
  RC-authored uid can collide; `:1088` prepends and carries every other set forward.
- `delete_stale_rc_item_sets` (`:1138`): `if not uid.startswith("RC-")` preserves
  unconditionally, BEFORE any RC scope test.
- `apply_item_set` `replace_all_rc` branch (`:1024`): even the nuclear option filters
  on `startswith("RC-")`.

The cap itself is `pushUnits.slice(0, 4)` at `web/js/panels/champ_select.js:2340`. It
bounds how many of RC's OWN builds get pushed, so truncation can only drop a 5th+ RC
build path - it has no mechanism to touch a user set. The filing INVERTS the direction:
the cap is a self-limit, not a global slot budget.

Already pinned by `tests/test_lcu_item_sets_wipe_stale.py:166`
`test_preserves_operator_custom_sets` and `:208` (4 current-scope `RC-` + 1 operator
custom = 5 kept) - the exact filed scenario is already regression-guarded. Ran
`tests/test_lcu_item_sets_wipe_stale.py` + `tests/test_csv_push_swap_wipe.py`:
**27 passed** (0.50s).

REAL RESIDUAL, re-filed rather than dropped: `:1088` does `new_sets + sets`, so RC
sets sort to the TOP of the client list and a user's set is pushed further DOWN the
dropdown. That is visual POSITION, not eviction, and the list is not length-capped
anywhere. If the operator's underlying complaint was ordering, it is a `sortrank` /
insertion-position item against `tools/lcu_agent.py:1088` and a genuinely different bug.

### CORRECTION 2026-07-19 (same session) - RM-106b is NOT closed. The "NO" verdict above is RETRACTED.

The RM-106b closure recorded earlier in this block measured the flag-OFF state and is
WRONG. Do not inherit it. What actually happened: `EnableReplayApi` was ABSENT from
`game.cfg` at probe time, so every `/liveclientdata/*` route 404'd. The operator then
launched LeagueDirector (`C:/Users/Administrator/Documents/LeagueDirector/`, created
19:55), which WROTE `EnableReplayApi=1` into
`C:/Riot Games/League of Legends/Config/game.cfg` line 18. Re-probed with the flag ON,
against the same actively-playing KIWI replay:

- `GET :2999/liveclientdata/allgamedata` -> **HTTP 200 / 19846 bytes**, `gameMode KIWI`,
  `gameTime 25.95`, **10 players**, each carrying `items`, `level`, `runes`, `scores`,
  `summonerSpells`, `position`, `team`.
- `/replay/playback`, `/replay/game`, `/replay/particles`, `/replay/render`,
  `/replay/sequence`, `/replay/recording`, `/replay/banners` all serve (GET, most POST).
- `GET /replay/playback` -> `{length: 1026.54, paused: false, seeking: false, speed: 1.0,
  time: 25.99}`.

**SEEK-AND-SAMPLE PROVEN (this is the load-bearing measurement, not an inference):**
`POST /replay/playback {"time":600.0,"paused":true,"seeking":true}` -> HTTP 200, then
`GET /liveclientdata/allgamedata` measured `gameTime` exactly **600.0**, with Leona at
level **12** (was 3) and **5** items (was 4), and populated K/D/A 9/7/13. The sampled
state follows the seek. So per-timestamp ITEM progression is reconstructable for KIWI by
seeking and diffing `allPlayers[].items` - which is precisely what RM-106a (LCU timeline)
and RM-106 (SGP) both CANNOT deliver.

**TWO REAL LIMITS, measured not assumed:**

1. **SKILL ORDER IS NOT RECOVERABLE.** `GET /liveclientdata/activeplayerabilities`
   returns **HTTP 400** during replay playback - there is no "active player" in a
   spectator context. Only `implementationDetails` comes back. Do not plan skill-order
   work on this route.
2. **ITEMS DO NOT COME FROM EVENTS.** `eventdata` at t=600 carried only `GameStart` (1),
   `ChampionKill` (7), `Multikill` (1). There is NO `ITEM_PURCHASED`. Item state must be
   SAMPLED per seek and diffed; the event stream will never carry it.

**HARD BOUNDS UNCHANGED and still binding:** exactly TWO `.rofl` files exist on disk
(`NA1-5592802194.rofl` 13.0 MB, `NA1-5604806601.rofl` 8.3 MB) and replays are
patch-locked, so this is a FORWARD-CAPTURE route that CANNOT backfill the ~2952-match
history. It requires the game client running with a replay actively playing, so it is an
interactive capture and NEVER a background job.

**PROCESS LESSON:** the earlier verdict was recorded with an explicit caveat naming the
untested flag, and that caveat is the only reason the error was caught within the hour.
A measured negative taken while a known gating flag is unverified is not a negative - it
is an untested configuration. Verify the gate BEFORE recording a closure.

**OPERATOR STATE NOTE:** the seek probe moved the replay to t=600 paused; playback was

## 2026-07-20 - RM-108 shipped, original spec relocated

Relocated verbatim from ROADMAP.md when RM-108 was marked SHIPPED (`a60d32e6`, LEDGER 966). Retained for context; its central premise was measured FALSE - all 56,896 occurrences land in display-prose keys, none in a numerically-read key.

- **RM-108 (original spec).** TWO CONFIRMED INSTANCES of one defect class, found a month apart by unrelated work: (1) Font of Life 8463's base heal is the literal token `@BaseHeal@` in all four vendored DDragon rune snapshots, which is why R136 pinned it at zero credit rather than seeding a guess; (2) measured 2026-07-19, DDragon's Morgana Q tooltip reads `Roots the first enemy hit for {{ rootduration }} seconds` while its `effectBurn` is all `'0'` and `vars` is empty - the field is NAMED but the number moved to an unpublished datavalues layer. Same shape: **a vendored feed carries an unresolved placeholder where a number should be, and nothing flags it.** This is strictly worse than stale data, because a naive parser reads 0.0 or the literal string and ships it silently. Shape: a check over vendored feeds for tokens matching `@[A-Za-z_]+@` and `{{ *[a-z_]+ *}}` in fields the engine reads numerically, emitting a registry of known-unresolved (feed, key, token) that a test pins - so a NEW unresolved token fails loudly while the known ones stay documented rather than re-litigated. Cheap, and it shares the guard's whole walk, which is why it belongs inside Lane 1 rather than as its own tool. **BEARS ON THE CC-DURATION CEILING (context, not a re-open):** the item-225 sweep called CC-duration-in-seconds a TRUE CEILING, and that was re-confirmed 2026-07-19 from three angles - CDragon carries only the TAG (`cc_tags: ["Trait_ImmobilizingCCSpell"]` on Morgana Q, no duration) because duration lives in the buff/script layer whose scripts 404; DDragon names it but ships zeros; Meraki is wiki-derived prose. Match volume cannot help - Match-V5 records only aggregate `timeCCingOthers` / `totalTimeCCDealt`, an un-invertible sum over an unknown ability mix, because games record OUTCOMES and CC duration is a static SPEC. The precision worth carrying: the ceiling is on STRUCTURED sources; the wiki-prose route is real and RC already has the pattern for it (RM-86's prose-seeded curated registry per the `_passive_damage_overrides.py` precedent). Do NOT re-scan the four upstream layers - that sweep is EXHAUSTED.

The Settled `.rofl` fence did NOT need opening and remains CLOSED.** A four-tier model, every tier measured: **T0** `.rofl` tail JSON (end-of-game, whole corpus, headless); **T1** Match-V5 frames (60 s); **T2** Match-V5 events (sub-second WITH map coords - `CHAMPION_KILL` carries a per-spell damage breakdown naming `spellName`/`spellSlot`, which was previously assumed Layer-2-only); **T3** `:2999` seek + camera back-projection (~19 map units, interactive one game at a time); **T4** differential rendering of paused frames. **FOUR MEASUREMENTS INVERTED THE BRIEF'S PREMISE.** (a) The v2 container has NO encryption - plain zstd, stdlib-openable, and the roflxd/Blowfish layout everyone cites is the older v1 container. The fence's CRYPTO rationale is void; its CHURN rationale stands and worsened (two builds inside patch 16.14) and the stream carries zero plaintext identifiers. (b) Sub-minute positions come from the sanctioned replay API: `cameraRotation` is `{x:YAW, y:PITCH}`, the camera looks `h/tan(p)` AHEAD of its own coordinates, `cameraPosition` is writable ONLY in `cameraMode:"fps"`, and an analytic ray/ground-plane solve gives **~19 units** self-consistency. (c) **Match-V5 60 s positions carry ~2000 units of error** (replicated on two games; 8 of 33 samples wrong by more than the 2750-unit decision threshold; a jungler standing ON a drake reported across the map), so `FAR_UNITS`/`SIGNAL_DECAY` in `core/replay_analysis.py` are historical-calibration only and are NOT facts about junglers. (d) Paused renders are BIT-DETERMINISTIC (0 px between identical renders), so flipping one entity toggle makes the pixel difference that entity class - **wave state** (minions, **4787 px re-measured 2026-07-26 under the warm-up - the original 11694 was 2.4x inflated by a method defect, but the capability stands: on-axis blobs land 64/7/92 units off the mid lane, and blob count is NOT wave size**) and **ward coverage** (both team colours render under fog-off; the original 13-blob count is NOT replicated at 2 blobs from a narrower pose, neither confirmed nor refuted) both unblock with no ML. Corpus 2026-07-26: 108 accounts / **417 `.rofl`, 334 distinct, 5.82 GB apparent but 4.67 GB on disk** (hardlink dedupe took ~20 pct), plus a timeline corpus whose ingest CLOSED at **3005 matches** (~116 KB per match vs ~13 MB, paginated arbitrarily deep with NO retention cutoff - that, not more `.rofl`, is how the corpus grows). `RC-ReplayChainWatch` owns the follow-ups a session used to hold and short-circuits while any ingest holds the rate budget, so `RC-ReplayRosterPull` Disabled with a non-empty `busy` is CORRECT, not a stuck watchdog. **OPEN / OWED:** (i) **B13 - CLOSED 2026-07-26. ## 2026-08-04 - RM-159 relocated verbatim (headless run 2026-08-04-01)

_Relocated from `ROADMAP.md` the same day it was filed, purely for the 80 KB CI budget (the file was at 98.7 percent). The row is CLOSED; this is the full evidence._

- **RM-159 CLOSED-BY-MEASUREMENT 2026-08-04 (headless run 2026-08-04-01) - DO NOT make `tools/stop_claim_gate.py` negation-aware. Two serious attempts, both REFUTED, and the approach is unsound rather than the attempts being sloppy.** The itch is real: the gate's `count_mismatch` (and 6 of its 9 checks) treat a RETRACTION as a fresh assertion, so "I have NOT observed 18226 passed" is flagged exactly like claiming it. Fixing that by inferring negation SCOPE from prose does not work. **Attempt 1 (`80ea4518`)** wired the helper into 8 of 9 checks, passed 32 of its own tests, passed the full suite, and ran a genuine mutation probe (its rule 8/8 where a naive rule scored 1/8) - an adversarial pass found **16 laundering phrases the UNMODIFIED gate flagged and the "fix" silenced** ("Without question 18226 passed", "I never doubted 18226 passed"). Root cause was the gate's own regex: `CLAIM_COUNT` carried an optional leading `(?:(\w+)\s+)?` group that SWALLOWED the content word before the number, so the scope span came out empty and short-circuited to "negation governs". **Attempt 2 (`eb76d1f9`)** fixed the source properly (removed the group, moved the ordinal filter to a lookbehind, passed explicit claim bounds), fixed all 16, ran **233 mechanism-derived probes** across 13 families, and had every one of its 7-8 guards individually mutation-killed. A single independent pass built from the opposite direction - read the five conditions, attack each - found **28 of 47 fresh phrases silenced, all 28 flagged by the pre-fix gate**. **The killer evidence is the one-word twins, which make this evasion-by-paraphrase and not an edge case:** `could not` FLAGS / `couldn't` SILENT (the `_NEG_MODAL` veto searches `sentence[:neg.start()]`, and in a contraction the modal is INSIDE the negation token, so the counterfactual veto can never fire); `could not` FLAGS / `ought not` SILENT (`ought`/`need`/`dare` absent from the modal list); `by accident` FLAGS / `by happenstance` SILENT (`_NEG_LITOTES` is a 5-word closed list). Also `No, 18226 passed` FLAGS but `No, I confirm 18226 passed` is SILENT - one transparent verb defeats the module's own stated promise. **The structural reason no third attempt should be authorised:** the gate audits the agent's OWN prose, and the agent writes the prose, so ANY prose-level inference is gameable by the writer - including an explicit retraction MARKER, which the same agent could equally emit. The gate's actual value is catching UNINTENTIONAL overclaim, and against that threat a strict gate is strictly better: it catches the honest mistake AND the retraction, where a negation-aware gate trades bypasses of the former for quieter handling of the latter. **DECISION (made under the run's full-authority grant, logged not gated): keep the gate STRICT and accept the retraction false positive.** It cost this run one line of acknowledgement per turn and zero work, against a measured 16 + 28 bypass surface. If the FP noise ever becomes intolerable, the ONLY acceptable direction is a change that cannot be expressed in the audited prose at all - e.g. the gate consuming a structured evidence record the agent cannot author as narration - not a better regex. Evidence: this row plus memory `feedback_mutation_probe_vs_naive_alternative`. Neither branch was merged; `git branch --contains` confirms both `80ea4518` and `eb76d1f9` exist only on their worktree branches.

It does NOT stream - it buffers with `body = r.read()` (`dashboard/_handler.py:226`) and its docstring contradicts itself in one sentence; an 8 MiB payload arrived byte-complete at a reader stalled 3s mid-stream because the send buffer absorbs the write and SO_SNDTIMEO never trips. **What a connection-lifetime timeout actually breaks is the READ side** - socketserver arms it in `setup()`, so it deadlines the request line and headers, and every 2 Hz poller opens a fresh HTTP/1.0 connection. Shipped `_BODY_READ_TIMEOUT_S = 10.0` armed narrowly around the body read (absolute budget, so a trickle client cannot re-arm it per byte), plus the DS side's missing 1 MiB cap refused ON THE HEADER, a 400 on non-numeric Content-Length, and the same deadline on `_drain_request_body`. **The sharp edge, worth keeping:** the body read runs BEFORE the auth gate, so ANY exception there is answered as 400 and pre-empts the 401 - a first attempt with an unguarded `sock = self.connection` did exactly that to all 7 `test_control_endpoint_auth.py` tests. The guard is `getattr(self, "connection", None)` with a fall-through, and a test now pins that a body-read failure cannot pre-empt the auth reply. The spec doc `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-31-mission-control-s10-decouple.md` was carrying the false premise forward into the unbuilt `:8895` and is corrected.

## 2026-08-06 (headless run 2026-08-06-02) - original filings relocated on closure

Relocate-only, verbatim. Each row below was closed or largely closed by run 2026-08-06-02;
its surviving verdict, fences and residuals stay in `ROADMAP.md`. Nothing here is open.

- **RM-163** ORIGINAL FILING, kept for its measurements: `core/riot_api.py` never caches a NEGATIVE result, so every Match-V5 consumer refires the same outbound call forever.** `core/riot_api.py:520-522` does `data = _call(...)` then `if data is not None: get_cache().set_immutable(...)`.
